quotes.text: What are the consequences of disseminating intelligence analysis derived from processes that nobody understands?

Now, the use of AI by the U.S. Intelligence Community raises many issues, starting with accountability. Now, if AI is going to inform the Intelligence Community's surveillance decisions, one question I would have is if an American is spied on in violation of the law, who is responsible?

I have proposed the Algorithm Accountability Act that would require that companies test their AI for harmful bias, such as biases that can affect where you buy a house or what healthcare you have access to.

The threat to Americans' privacy is even more serious when you stop to consider the discussion about artificial intelligence and how artificial intelligence can be used against enormous amounts of commercially available data, including location information on Americans.

There is another example of secret law related to section 702, and it affects the privacy rights of the American people. [...] I strongly believe that this matter should be declassified and that Congress needs to debate it openly before 702 is reauthorized.

I want to talk, for example, about the implications of artificial intelligence on this debate, and these are fairly new developments that I think most Senators have not heard. The CEO of one of America's largest AI companies sounded this warning several weeks ago. He did it in a message about his firm's multimillion-dollar contract with the Department of Defense.

I am going to close with one last important issue that colleagues are approaching all of us to ask about, and that is the role of AI in supercharging surveillance abuses. [...] In the case of section 702, the government could use artificial intelligence to process huge amounts of data to identify Americans for warrantless searches. [...] New tools require new rules, and it really applies to artificial intelligence.
